  • 30th Annual Leaside Rotary Corn Roast returns Sept 20
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-09-17
    A longtime Leaside tradition returns to Trace Manes Park on Sunday, September 20, as the Rotary Club of Toronto-Leaside hosts its 30th annual Community Corn Roast. Running from noon to 4:30 p.m., the free community event will feature face painting, inflatables, a fish pond, family games and a BBQ. The Corn Roast takes place at Trace Manes Park, at McRae Drive and Millwood Road. Admission is free. For more information, visit the Rotary Club of Toronto-Leaside .

    A new centre for travel has arrived at 2507 Yonge Street (near Keewatin Ave). No matter where you want to go or what you want to experience, the Travel Experts at Flight Centre Crosstown can help you plan your next adventure. For more information and store hours, visit Flight Centre Crosstown .

  • Storm brings an unexpected engagement in Leaside
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-09-05
    Following the recent CTV News report on Leaside’s traffic woes , here’s a happier neighbourhood story from Global News. A massive maple limb came crashing down onto a Leaside home during Wednesday afternoon’s storm, blocking the front door and sidewalk — just as homeowner Stephen Armstrong was preparing to propose to his girlfriend of six years. The storm didn’t derail his plans. Global News has the storm damage, the proposal and a very relieved newly engaged couple (she said yes!) — full story here .

  • STOP means STOP: Traffic concerns grow in Leaside
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-09-04
    Leaside is in the news for all the wrong reasons. CTV News reports on concerns about speeding and drivers ignoring stop signs on neighbourhood streets, following a recent collision at Millwood Road and Hanna Road that sent a child to hospital. Residents say the problem is nothing new, and are calling for more to be done to slow drivers down. From the Bulldog archives: Some things haven’t changed. Back in 2015, we spoke with then-Ward 26 Councillor Jon Burnside at the corner of Hanna Road and Millwood Road about drivers ignoring stop signs in Leaside. Burnside was calling on the City to investigate camera-based enforcement as a way to change driver behaviour.

  • After six decades, a sad farewell to Bayview Car Wash
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-08-28
    Handwritten “Permanently Closed” signs are now posted at Bayview Car Wash at 1802 Bayview Ave. — a neighbourhood fixture. The closure has been coming for some time. As we reported last year , the Ontario Land Tribunal approved plans for a 46-storey mixed-use development on the property at Bayview and Roehampton. The approved plans called for 441 residential units along with ground-floor non-residential space. Redevelopment is moving ahead: the City issued a demolition permit in June for the existing car wash, with the work described as making way for environmental remediation ahead of future development. For generations of local drivers, the old-school Bayview Car Wash — with its unmistakable roadside sign — was simply part of the landscape. Time marches on. Thanks for 62 years of clean cars, Bayview Car Wash — we’ll miss you. Application Details OLT approves 46 storeys at Bayview Car Wash site UrbanToronto: 1802 Bayview Avenue

  • Notice of Refusal of Official Plan Amendment and Passing of Zoning By-law - 922 Millwood Road
    City of Toronto public notices (City Clerk) ·Leaside ·2026-08-14
    NOTICE OF REFUSAL OF OFFICIAL PLAN AMENDMENT AND ZONING BY-LAW AMENDMENT APPLICATION (Under the Planning Act) TAKE NOTICE that the City of Toronto on July 30, 2026, refused a request to amend the Official Plan and refused an application to amend the Zoning By-law, with respect to the lands known as 922 Millwood Road. An explanation of the purpose and effect of the requested amendment to the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendment application, and a map showing the location of the lands to which the amendments apply, are attached. The amendments were processed under file: 25 227957 NNY 15 OZ. A statutory public meeting was held on July 7, 2026, and the North York Community Council and Toronto City Council considered four oral and 83 written submissions in making the decision.   • The Bayview shuffle: Signs of change along Bayview Avenue
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-08-11
    A few changes to report along Bayview Avenue… Fiorio Hair Salon is now Teilah Salon at 1541 Bayview Ave., with new signage and branding now up at the storefront. More information is available at teilah.ca . New store alert: Gather Mercantile has moved into 1579 Bayview Ave., in the former Modella Ladieswear location. The new shop describes itself as “Curated living. Proudly Canadian.” Follow Gather Mercantile on Instagram for updates. Modella closed its Bayview location earlier this year, while its other stores remain open. Now open: Myocare RMT + Wellness has opened its new Leaside clinic at 1517A Bayview Ave., above LIT Espresso Bar. The clinic offers registered massage therapy, acupuncture and osteopathic manual treatment, along with services including TMJ, lymphatic drainage and prenatal and postnatal massage. Bayview Vision has consolidated its two Bayview locations into its flagship store at 1709 Bayview Ave. We have been told that Vizio Eyewear clients can still find Lynn at the 1709 location. As reported earlier this year, the team at Bayview Vision took over care at the former Leaside Eye Clinic following the passing of longtime local optometrist Dr. Jonathan Slivka. Read our February update here . If you spotted the new signage at 1532 Bayview before Vizio closed, there’s a little more to that story. A housewares pop-up briefly shared the space with Vizio for a couple of weeks before Bayview Vision ultimately consolidated its operations at its main location. Meanwhile, a new antiques shop is taking shape at 1532 Bayview. Work is underway to transform the former optical displays and cabinetry for their new purpose. More details as they become available. There’s also something goin’ on inside 1560B Bayview Ave., the former 9Round kickboxing studio. We spotted a “leased” sign there back in March , and there are now signs of activity inside — but still no word on who’s moving in. And one more to keep an eye on: community chatter on social media suggests that a popular Toronto pizza chain may be heading to Bayview. Nothing confirmed yet, so we’ll leave that one in the rumour file for now. Spotted something new in the neighbourhood? Photos and tips are always welcome — send them our way through the Bulldog contact form .

    NOTICE OF PASSING OF ZONING BY-LAW 1230-2026 (Under the Planning Act) TAKE NOTICE that the City of Toronto passed Zoning By-law 1230-2026 on July 30, 2026, with respect to the lands known as 148, 158 and 162 Soudan Avenue. An explanation of the purpose and effect of the Zoning By-law, and a map showing the location of the lands to which the amendment applies, are attached. The amendment was processed under file number: 25 135273 STE 12 OZ. A statutory public meeting was held on July 8 and 9, 2026, and the Toronto and East York Community Council and Toronto City Council considered three oral and three written submissions in making the decision. Please see item TE34.28 at https://secure.toronto.ca/council/agenda-item.do?item=2026.TE34.28 . IF YOU WISH TO APPEAL TO THE ONTARIO LAND TRIBUNAL: Take notice that an appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal in respect to all or part of this Zoning By-law may be made by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk, Attention: Raneisha Hemmings, Registrar Secretariat, 100 Queen Street West, 2nd Floor West, Toronto, ON, M5H 2N2, no later than 4:30 p.m. on August 25, 2026. If delivering in-person, drop off at the Registry Services Counter, Toronto City Hall. The

    Leaside Business Park Association ·Leaside ·2026-08-03
    Business Resource Spotlight As part of our commitment to connecting businesses with valuable resources, the LBPA regularly highlights programs and services that can help businesses grow and succeed. Businesses in the Leaside Business Park have access to a wide range of free programs and services offered by the City of Toronto. Whether you’re planning to expand, relocate, invest, or simply want to better understand the resources available to your business, the City’s Business Expansion and Location Assistance team can help connect you with the right information and support. Services include: – Business expansion guidance – Site selection assistance – Investment information – Connections to City departments – Economic development resources If you’re considering growing your business, it’s worth exploring the services available. Learn more on the City of Toronto website: https://www.toronto.ca/business-economy/business-operation-growth/business-expansion-and-location-assistance/ The post City of Toronto Services to Help Your Business Grow appeared first on Leaside Business Park .

  • Pedestrian scramble approved for bustling Yonge & Eg.
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-07-30
    Toronto City Council has approved plans for a pedestrian “scramble intersection” at Yonge & Eglinton, one of the busiest intersections in the city. The installation is expected in 2027. A scramble intersection (also known as a pedestrian scramble or pedestrian priority phase ) is a traffic signal that temporarily stops all vehicle traffic, allowing pedestrians to cross in every direction at once — including diagonally. During the scramble phase, no vehicles are permitted to move through the intersection. Council also considered a second scramble intersection at Yonge St. and Roehampton Ave./Orchard View Blvd., but has directed staff to undertake further evaluation before moving ahead. For more on the decision, including why it was approved, potential impacts on traffic, and comments from city officials and transportation experts, see the full CityNews reporting .

  • Transit infrastructure capacity and development
    Federation of North Toronto Residents' Associations ·Unmatched ·2026-07-28
    FoNTRA strongly supports the Toronto City Council Member Motion that essentially requests the TTC to comment on development applications regarding the ability of transit to accommodate, both through station capacity and line capacity, the cumulative impacts of developments. In addition the Motion directs City staff to develop strategies for funding transit infrastructure growth requirements that support City approved development.

  • Addressing moribund development sites
    Federation of North Toronto Residents' Associations ·Unmatched ·2026-07-28
    FoNTRA strongly supports the Toronto City Council Member Motion that directs staff to undertake a comprehensive review of the City’s ability to manage “moribund sites”.   • Orange skies over Bayview-Leaside as smoke moves in
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-07-15
    Bayview-Leaside residents woke up Wednesday to an orange-yellow glow filtering through their windows as smoke from wildfires in northwestern Ontario settled over much of southern Ontario, prompting an air quality warning from Environment Canada. Similar smoky conditions affected the city last June , though Wednesday’s haze was particularly striking. The smoky conditions have been noticeable across the GTA, with hazy skies and reduced visibility. On Wednesday morning, Toronto ranked as the world’s most polluted major city on IQAir’s real-time air quality index . Environment Canada says the smoke could linger into Friday in some areas. Residents are being advised to limit time outdoors where possible, especially older adults, young children, pregnant people, those with heart or lung conditions, and people who work outdoors. Even healthy individuals may notice eye, nose or throat irritation, headaches or coughing. The air quality warning comes as southern Ontario also remains under a heat warning, making it even more important to stay cool indoors where possible. Current air quality information and health advice are available from Environment Canada’s Air Quality Health Index and its air quality warnings page . Related: Global News: Toronto’s air quality ranked world’s worst as wildfire smoke settles in • Accuweather: ‘Dangerous’ air quality in Detroit, Minneapolis as thick wildfire smoke shrouds the sky for millions .
    Read the original → The South Bayview Bulldog

  • Ruby Gala celebrates 40 years of Children’s Garden School
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-07-07
    A summer update from Children’s Garden School. Children’s Garden School recently celebrated its 40th anniversary with the Ruby Gala, held at Motorista Studio in Leaside. The evening brought together current and former families, staff and supporters to mark four decades of the school’s commitment to early childhood education while raising funds for future improvements. The school thanked founder and principal Marie Bates for her leadership over the past 40 years, as well as the many volunteers who helped make the event possible. Special recognition was given to the CGS Foundation Board, led by Chair Katrina Connolly, together with Sophia Wu, Lisa Cho and Alan Koutsaris, and to the Gala Committee for organizing the celebration. The evening also featured a live auction led by Rob Marsh and Mike Babcock, with organizers reporting that fundraising exceeded its goal thanks to the generosity of school families and supporters. The CGS Foundation is a volunteer-run charitable organization that supports Children’s Garden School by funding facilities, equipment, furnishings, teaching resources and other enhancements that enrich the student experience. Proceeds from this year’s Ruby Gala will support a number of projects across the school, including improvements to learning and community spaces. Fundraising will also help fund a new rock climbing wall in the gym, creating another opportunity for students to build strength, confidence and resilience. Congratulations to Children’s Garden School on its 40th anniversary and a successful Ruby Gala!

  • Paid Summer Student Outreach Role with LBPA
    Leaside Business Park Association ·Leaside ·2026-07-02
    The Leaside Business Park Association (LBPA) is hiring Student Outreach Ambassadors for a short-term paid summer role supporting local businesses during Ontario Line construction. This part-time role will support Phase Three of LBPA’s Transit Construction Mitigation project. Student Outreach Ambassadors will help visit and/or contact businesses in the Leaside Business Park area, collect updated business contact information, share information about the LBPA Traffic Alerts platform, and support local business visibility and communication. The goal of this work is to help businesses stay informed, accessible, and connected during construction, while helping LBPA build a more complete and up-to-date business contact database. This role is a good fit for students who are professional, organized, comfortable speaking with business owners and staff, and interested in business, communications, urban planning, transportation, community engagement, local economic development, or public affairs. Role details Compensation: $25/hour Estimated commitment: approximately 60–70 hours per student Timing: July and August 2026 Location: Leaside Business Park and surrounding area Deadline to apply: July 8, 2026 Apply here: https://forms.gle/iCqiN4vx4mMpwboU6 Full student role description: Leaside Business Park Student Outreach Ambassador Short-Term Summer Role The Leaside Business Park Association (LBPA) is looking for Student Outreach Ambassador to support Phase Three of its Transit Construction Mitigation Fund project. This short-term summer role will support business outreach across the Leaside Business Park and surrounding area. The goal is to help local businesses stay informed, accessible, and visible during Ontario Line construction, while helping LBPA build a more complete and up-to-date business contact database. Student Outreach Ambassador will conduct preliminary research in advance of scheduled outreach activities, then connect with local businesses through in-person visits and phone outreach. They will gather key business and operational contact information, introduce businesses to the Leaside Business Park Association (LBPA) and its Traffic Alerts platform, and help identify organizations that would benefit from additional engagement or follow-up. Through these efforts, Student Outreach Ambassador will play a key role in strengthening relationships within the loca…

  • Comedy Kicks! brings laughs to Mount Pleasant Village
    The South Bayview Bulldog ·Leaside ·2026-06-17
    The Mount Pleasant Village Comedy Festival returns this summer with a new soccer-themed title, Comedy Kicks!! , featuring free outdoor performances by stand-up comedians, improvisers and magicians. The shows will take place at 700 Mount Pleasant Rd. (at Soudan Ave.) on six consecutive Thursday evenings beginning June 18, from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. A free family-friendly Kids Day performance starring WonderPhil is also scheduled for Saturday, June 20 at 10 a.m. The lineup includes improv performances by Comedy Bar All-Stars, stand-up comedy featuring several Toronto comics, and a comedy magic show with Matt DiSero. Seating is outdoors, with a rain location across the street at Granite Brewery, 245 Eglinton Ave. E. Comedy Kicks!! is presented by Mount Pleasant Village BIA with help from our supporters, The Briton House Retirement Home, Granite Brewery and the City of Toronto through the Community Celebration Support Fund. For the full schedule and details, visit mountpleasantvillage.ca/comedy .

    Leaside Residents Association ·Leaside ·2026-05-15
    The LRA is holding a Town Hall on Tuesday, May 26, at 7:30 p.m. (doors 7:15 p.m.), at the William Lea Room, Leaside Memorial Community Gardens. Join us for a discussion of the recent Leaside community survey results, featuring Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin. The Q& A will be joined by LRA co-presidents on issues facing Leaside now and in the future. Please note that due to unforeseen circumstances, the Annual General Meeting previously scheduled to precede the Town Hall is postponed. Stay tuned for a new date!

  • Student Bursaries from 53 Division – Toronto Police
    South Eglinton Davisville Residents' Association (SEDRA) ·Davisville ·2026-04-25
    The Toronto Police 53 Division Community Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) is offering its annual Student Leadership Bursary Awards, provided to graduating high school students that live or go to school within the 53 Division boundaries. Students must demonstrate financial need and will be attending post-secondary programs and/or training programs at either Ontario publicly-assisted colleges or universities. The value of each bursary is $3,000.00. Eligibility: Graduating Grade 12 Student Canadian citizen, permanent resident or otherwise entitled to study in Canada Lives or goes to school within the 53 Division Boundaries Received acceptance to a certificate program, part-time undergraduate degree program, or full-time undergraduate degree program in 2026-27 academic year Demonstrates financial need, academic achievement, exceptional community service and extracurricular involvement Applications must also include: A completed Student Leadership Bursary Awards Application Form. Please fill out this PDF form electronically. A Personal Statement (maximum of 1000 words) outlining your financial need, lived experiences, accomplishments, community leadership/volunteer involvement in the community, career goals and how this bursary will help you. Two Reference Letters Up-to-date Resume Proof of Acceptance and Enrolment to Post-Secondary Program/Training Institute Deadline: May 10, 2026 SUBMIT YOUR ELECTRONIC REGISTRATION TO: 53.Division@tps.ca FOR MORE INFORMATION: Tim Somers: 416‐808‐5337 Application Forms may be downloaded here: 53 Division Student Leadership Bursary Awards_FORM_2026 Download

  • You’re Invited to SEDRA’s 2026 AGM!
    South Eglinton Davisville Residents' Association (SEDRA) ·Davisville ·2026-04-23
    South Eglinton Davisville Residents’ Association (SEDRA) invites you to our 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM). When: Tuesday, May 5, 2026 Event Start: 6:30pm, Starting with Annual General Meeting proceedings, with Town Hall & Special Guest Speakers/Panel to follow Event End: Between 8:30-9:00pm Where: Manor Rd United, 240 Manor Road East (at Forman) Featuring: Councillors Josh Matlow and Rachel Chernos Lin Keynote Speaker/Moderator: John Lorinc New This Year: All attendees will have the chance to win a door prize – one of John Lorinc’s books! All are welcome at the event – as well, current SEDRA members are able to vote during the AGM. In order to plan accordingly, we kindly ask you to RSVP by requesting free tickets through the below Eventbrite link. You are not required to bring a printout of your ticket to the event; it is only to anticipate attendance. To renew or enrol as a SEDRA Member for 2026 and take part in voting during the AGM, click here . To RSVP: Get your free tickets here Photo: Chair of Tall/Midrise Working Group Jeff Latto presents at previous AGM Photo Credit: Charles Iscove John Lorinc is a Toronto journalist and editor who writes about cities, planning, local history, business and climate change. He is a regular contributor to The Globe and Mail , the Toronto Star , Spacing and Corporate Knights. John is the author of five books, including No Jews Live Here: A Memoir, and has co-edited several editions of Coach House Books’ uTOpia series, among them, “The Ward: The Life and Loss of Toronto’s First Immigrant Neighbourhood,” and “Messy Cities: Why We Can’t Plan Everything. “ In preparation for the event, John has shared his list of notable planning/development moments from the past decade: late-2010s — Housing Now strategy adopted by former Mayor John Tory, now seeing construction 2019 — Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods, allowing laneway suites, garden suites, multiplexes, small apartment buildings on major streets and small-scale retail in neighbourhoods Early 2020s — Condo speculation boom, enabled by the pandemic and historically low interest rates MTSAs — enactment of provincial transit-oriented development policies in the form of intensification zones/secondary plans around rapid transit stations, along with (weak) inclusionary zoning policies Post-2023 — city’s decision to establish its own development agencies, advance c…

  • Major Transit Station Areas (MSTAs) in our Local Neighbourhood
    South Eglinton Davisville Residents' Association (SEDRA) ·Davisville ·2026-03-31
    In August 2025, the Province approved Toronto’s Major Transit Station Areas (MTSAs) and Protected Major Transit Station Areas (PMTSAs). These are defined areas within roughly a 10-minute walk of transit hubs (subway stations, GO stations and streetcar stops). There are now 120 of these areas across the city, collectively known as P/MTSAs. Inside these areas, the Province requires that the City plan for growth and development through updated zoning. In principle, these 120 new P/MTSAs replace the previous five growth areas (Downtown, Islington-Bloor, Scarborough Centre, Yonge-Sheppard and, of course, Yonge-Eglinton). This should reduce the concentration of development we have traditionally seen in these five areas. Likewise, there should be an increase in development in areas close to transit hubs that are outside of the traditional growth centres. The SEDRA-area map below shows two zones defined in the P/MTSA legislation of 200-metre and 500-metre zones around the Davisville, Eglinton, Mount Pleasant and Leaside subway stations. The dark blue zone represents 200 meters from a transit hub, and the light blue represents 500 metres. The black outline shows the full extent of each MTSA area around the four transit hubs. These station areas were initially identified in the City Planning report dated March 4, 2022. The tricky part is that while these two colours represent different degrees of permitted density and building heights, these zones must be seen in combination with land uses of the City’s Official Plan, as shown below. The result is that the four land uses in our neighbourhood (i.e., Mixed-use, Apartment Neighbourhood, Neighbourhoods and Parks/Open Space) will be conditioned on whether a property is within 200 metres (dark blue) or 500 metres (light blue) of a transit hub. What the City is working on now It goes without saying that the overlay of various planning regimes on top of each other can lead to confusion. City Planning is currently drafting the zoning by-law changes needed to implement development permissions within the P/MTSAs, while respecting Land Uses defined in the City’s Official Plan. These bylaws will define rules around parking, setbacks, angular planes, massing and density, and are expected to go to Council this spring for approval. Here is what we know so far from both the Province and the City: Mixed Use Areas and Apartment Neighbo…

  • EFT Available for Membership and Donation
    South Eglinton Davisville Residents' Association (SEDRA) ·Davisville ·2026-03-25
    By popular demand, SEDRA now offers the option to use bank transfer (EFT) to make payment for your membership , or to make a donation . To pay by bank transfer (EFT), please set SEDRA as a payee in your online banking, using the email address payments@sedratoronto.ca Please include your name, email address and postal (street) address in the message box for the transfer. Note that we have auto-deposit set up, so no security question is needed. Your payment will be automatically deposited to our bank account. Payment by PayPal or credit card remains available. Please visit the membership or donation pages by clicking the links, in order to get access to the associated payment links. You may also continue to pay by cheque if you prefer. Please mail your cheque to: South Eglinton Davisville Residents’ Association PO Box 43613, 1601 Bayview Ave, Toronto, ON M4G 4G8 Please ensure that your name and address is on the cheque or include a covering note.
